_about: 777-8, built from the 777-9's measured outlines (b779/, Boeing D6-86073 Rev G 2.2.1; Boeing has published no general-dimensions sheet of the 777-8) with its two fuselage plugs taken out: plug.py on b779's snapped lines (side.snap.json, plan.snap.json; --ppm 69.8178, --nose 159 side and 167 plan, --plug 17.0:-3.734 --plug 44.3:-2.133), the front view as it is. Pixels of the 777-9's rasters. The plugs: 5.867 m in all, Boeing's 777-8 overall length (232 ft 6 in, 70.86 m: boeing.com's 777X page, the 777-8F Airport Compatibility Brochure) against the 777-9's (251 ft 9 in), the same tail; 3.734 m of it (12 ft 3 in) ahead of the main gear, the two types' printed wheelbases (93 ft 10 in on the 777-8F brochure and on the 2015 777X brochure's 777-8X, 106 ft 1 in on the 777-9), and the rest, 2.133 m, aft of it: 7 and 4 of the 777's 21 in frame pitches. The 777-8F brochure's door 1 (22 ft 2 in) and forward cargo door (38 ft 9 in) are the 777-9's, so the forward plug is behind them; its lower aft cargo door (157 ft 9 in) is the 777-9's large aft cargo door (177 ft 1 in) less the whole 5.867 m. Where in those stretches the plugs go isn't published for the 777-8: the forward one ahead of door 2 and the aft one between door 3 and the optional exit, as the 2015 777X brochure's 777-8X servicing plan draws its doors (door 2 at its passenger bridge, about 19.3 m; tabs on both sides at about 38.9 m, 43.2 m and 54.9 m: door 3, the exit and door 4 of a 777-9 with its plugs out, the aft one then 1.07 m shorter). Door 3 (42.72 m on the 777-9, door table 2.7.1) is hidden behind the flaps on the 777-9's sheet, so it's placed from the table, as wide as door 2, with the four windows round it left out (the -9 sheet's window gap round door 2). Windows: the 777-9's (drawn), moved with the plugs. Cockpit panes: the 777-9 sheet draws its windshield small and up to 18 cm below the crown, so the two don't meet over the nose; the 777X keeps the 777's flight deck, so the panes are the 777-300ER's (shapes/B77W.json, whose nose lies within 4 cm of this one's), in these pixels, as the 777-9's recipe now takes them, the windshield's forward edge put on this crown by build.py's rule.

windows.note: The 777-9's windows as its sheet draws them (D6-86073 2.2.1), moved with the 777-8's two plugs (7 and 4 windows out at the 0.533 m pitch); four left out round door 3, which the 777-9's sheet hides behind the flaps. No drawing of the 777-8's own cabin is published.

sources.title: Boeing, 777-9 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-86073 Rev G, September 2025, preliminary information), 2.2.1 General Dimensions: Model 777-9, and 2.7.1 Door Locations
sources.note: The outlines are the 777-9's (shapes/B779.json, tools/trace/b779/) with the 777-8's two fuselage plugs taken out (tools/trace/b778/): the same wing, GE9X nacelles, tail and fuselage section, which every Boeing 777-8 source says it shares. Its door table (2.7.1) places door 3 (42.72 m on the 777-9), which the sheet's side view hides behind the flaps. Fuselage height, width, tailplane span and engine position are the 777-9's printed figures. Its table puts all three lower cargo doors, the bulk door included, on the right (as D6-58329-2's 777-200LR/-300ER cargo-door figure draws them).

sources.title: Boeing, 777-8F Airport Compatibility Brochure (June 2023, preliminary), size comparisons, door location comparisons, landing gear footprint
sources.note: The 777-8 passenger aircraft has the 777-8F's fuselage length (Boeing, 2023). Overall length 232 ft 6 in (70.86 m), span 235 ft 5 in (71.76 m), wheelbase 93 ft 10 in (106 ft 1 in on the 777-9): the plugs, 3.734 m ahead of the main gear and 2.133 m behind it. Door 1 at 22 ft 2 in and the forward cargo door at 38 ft 9 in, as the 777-9's; the lower aft cargo door at 157 ft 9 in, the 777-9's large one less both plugs.

sources.title: Boeing, 777X (boeing.com product page): 777-8 and 777-9 dimensions
sources.note: 777-8 length 232 ft 6 in (70.9 m), 777-9 251 ft 9 in (76.7 m); the same wingspan (235 ft 5 in extended, 212 ft 9 in folded) and height (64 ft 1 in).

sources.title: Boeing, 777X Airport Compatibility Brochure (May 2015, preliminary), 777-8X general arrangement and servicing arrangement
sources.note: The 777-8 as first designed (69.8 m, 1.07 m shorter behind the wing than today's; the same 93 ft 10 in wheelbase). Its servicing plan places door 2 at its passenger bridge (about 19.3 m from the nose) and draws door tabs on both sides at about 38.9, 43.2 and 54.9 m: the 777-9's door 3, optional exit and door 4 with the plugs out, so the forward plug is ahead of door 2 and the aft one between door 3 and the exit. Read off a small plan view, to about 0.3 m. The door positions here follow from that, not from a 777-8 door table (none is published): confidence low.
